sequences.summary: This is one continuous live attacking sequence. Red works around the far end boards and crowded crease; the opening carrier and transfer toward the net are partly obscured. Play then moves right, with red T4 and white T2 pursuing and contesting the ball in the corner. It subsequently comes down the near boards toward red T9, later T14, and white T1. Their challenge sends the ball left into open floor by frame 142. The later context shows the continuing leftward chase and eventual white T12 control near midcourt. The running clock and continued pursuit do not indicate a stoppage or an official holding the ball. No goal or definite shot outcome is established.

A near-board contest in front of the right-hand goal sends the pink/red ball loose toward the left. White recover through the T1/T12 group, with T12 emerging as the carrier through center. A likely forward pass reaches T1 near the far boards; white then appear to move the ball inward to T15. T19 pressures T15, who shields the ball and works laterally right rather than immediately shooting. Subsequent context supports continued white possession and a developing chance at the left goal, where the goalkeeper drops to defend. No stoppage, official-held ball, or confirmed goal is established. Estimates account for the camera pan; several short transfers have uncertain release timing.

This is a continuous white-team attack on the left goal. Possession appears to shift from pressured T15 on the right to T1, who cuts inward and sends a low attempt toward the crease around frames 322–338. T14 drops into the lane and goalkeeper T21 sprawls; neither a goal nor a cover is established. T12 follows the live ball left of the net, retrieves it along the boards, and turns back across the front, apparently continuing under fragment T26. Red defenders converge on that drive. The ball emerges loose into the near-side lane by 428 and rolls diagonally left through 442. Context at 450–458 shows white T25 reaching it near the boards. There is no clear stoppage within the targets; the later period graphic is a cut, not a continuation of the ball path.

The ball emerges from traffic near the left goal and rolls toward the near-left boards. White T25 catches up while red T13 pressures from behind. A full-screen second-period graphic then breaks play continuity; the later center faceoff is not a continuation of that ball path. After the edit, the central official likely holds the ball until the faceoff around frame 555. The ensuing touch sends play rightward into red's defensive end, briefly beyond the camera. Red T37 retreats toward the ball with white T33 pursuing. T37's low stick provides a plausible ball location, although the ball may still be rolling farther ahead toward the corner. No goal is established by this sequence.

Following the center restart, play moves into the red team's right defensive corner. T37 retrieves the ball with white T33 pursuing. Their corner challenge is followed by movement across the red end toward the far-side red defender, appearing as T40/T42; the exact release and route are less certain than the receiving area. The ball then moves up the far boards toward T47, where T43 applies pressure. It is subsequently recycled to T42, who retreats along the end boards toward the back of his own goal. The later context supports this continued possession rather than a separate play. Goalkeeper T38/T49 remains at the goal; no definite shot, save, goal, stoppage, or official-held ball is established.

Red retreats along the far boards into its own right-end corner under white pressure. T42 then appears to send an outlet left along the wall, leading to the T52/T53 contest around frames 780–788. The subsequent leftward transfer is less certain: white T56 is the likely eventual receiver, with red T39 pursuing, but a brief red carry remains an alternative. Around 855–870, play reverses rightward and white T58 receives or collects the ball in the middle lane. T58 advances toward the far-side blue line as red T55 and T61 close; later context supports white continuing the attack along the far wall. No clear stoppage, official-held ball, shot, or goal is established.

White advances from neutral court into the right attacking end, with T58 carrying along the far boards under red pressure. T58 then works the ball inside to T54; the precise release/reception timing around frames 938–952 is obscured. T54 draws T55 and passes diagonally to near-side T59, who controls before returning the ball left toward T66. T66 negotiates T61's low challenge and advances toward goal while T61 falls. Subsequent context shows the goalkeeper dropping amid converging net-front players, but does not establish a goal. No separate restart is visible within the requested interval.

White T59's lateral feed reaches T66 on the left. T66 advances past the sliding T61, then sends the ball toward the screened goalmouth around 1058–1072 as goalkeeper T63/T70 drops. Play stops, and the subsequent retrieval motion near red T55 favors the ball having remained at or inside the net; the actual goal-line crossing is not resolved. During the stoppage, the ball is lofted leftward from the goal area, visibly high at 1140 and 1155 and near or above the image boundary between them. It descends near the white-player cluster and T60, who appears to guide it left with his blade afterward. No restart is visible.

The requested interval is a stoppage, not a live attack. White players gather and then walk toward the far-side bench while red players disperse and the goalkeeper remains near the net. The ball is most plausibly held by the striped official beside the white group, although its early hand location is unresolved. That official appears to lob it toward the nearer official: a small pink/red ball is visible aloft at 1290, followed by the nearer official reaching overhead at 1298. The receiving official likely retains it afterward. The final camera pan leaves that official and ball off-screen; there is no evidence of a restart or of possession returning to the goalkeeper.

This sequence shows a continuing stoppage, not an active attack. Players and officials disperse before the camera pans toward the red goalkeeper and the scoreboard, whose clock remains at 9:23. The goalkeeper adjusts position and equipment without a supported ball interaction. The camera returns left around frames 1455–1485, revealing players assembling at center for a restart. The ball is most plausibly with a restart official, outside the image during the goalkeeper view, then concealed in the center official's hand area. No pass, shot, faceoff drop, or scoring outcome is established in the supplied frames.

The opening camera pan leaves the waiting red goalkeeper and settles on center rink during an existing stoppage. Throughout all requested frames, players arrange themselves for a restart while the central striped official, briefly labeled T102, waits, gestures, and then moves closer to the centers. The ball is not cleanly resolved; its most plausible location is in this official's hand, initially near torso height and subsequently lowered toward the hip. The regions account for uncertainty about the holding hand. No ball drop, live possession, pass, shot, or restart is established, including in the following context through frame 1688. The cause of the stoppage is not established.

The requested interval shows a prolonged center-court stoppage and faceoff preparation, not active stickhandling. The ball is most plausibly held by the central official, frequently screened by red #50/T97 and the surrounding players. The camera shifts left around frame 1680, and the official changes position within the group. Players settle into faceoff stances near the end. The release occurs around the transition to frame 1800; its exact timing is unresolved. Subsequent context shows a brief contest, followed by red #50/T97 collecting the pink ball and moving left by frame 1822. No shot or goal is established. Target-frame locations are inferred hand regions rather than confirmed ball pixels.

A center faceoff develops into a brief stick battle. Red T97 emerges with the ball and advances along the near-side lane while white defenders retreat. T112 challenges near the attacking blue line, and T97 appears to shoot toward the left goal around frames 1860–1868. The goalkeeper drops, but the ball's contact with the goalkeeper or goal is not resolved. Subsequent movement suggests recovery toward the far-side corner by red T101, followed by possible circulation behind the goal toward T96, with T99 defending. Those later touches are substantially less certain than the initial carry. No goal or subsequent stoppage is established.

This appears to be one continuous red-team attack, followed by a stoppage. After the right-board action, the ball most likely travels behind the left goal with red T96, subsequently associated with T117 and T119. T97 along the left wall is an alternative early controller. The behind-net attacker reverses direction and emerges on the right, then sends a delivery toward the crowded crease/slot. T101 closes on the goal, and the goalkeeper drops and sprawls during the ensuing challenge. Play is stopped by approximately 2055–2062; subsequent frames show players waiting and officials approaching, not a new possession. The ball is most plausibly covered or retained around the goalkeeper. Neither a goal nor a transfer to an official is clearly established. Most locations below are motion-constrained inferences, not clean visual detections of the pink ball.

All requested targets belong to one stoppage around the left-hand goal, not an ongoing pass or shot. Earlier context shows the goalkeeper down and players disengaging. The unseen ball is initially most plausibly secured in the goalkeeper's glove/pad area. The far-side official approaches the crease, then leaves toward the near-left restart area; a goalkeeper-to-official collection around frames 2160–2190 is plausible, but the exchange is hidden. Later context shows players arranging for a faceoff, supporting official-held ball estimates rather than floor locations. Camera panning accounts for much of the early image-position change. Neither a goal nor the exact cause of the stoppage is established.

All requested frames belong to a stoppage and faceoff setup, not continuous live-ball possession. Players leave the left-goal area and take positions while the left-side official approaches the faceoff location and signals; the other official moves right. The ball is not individually resolved, but is most plausibly held by the faceoff official, usually in the lower/drop hand, with some uncertainty about which hand. Later context shows the official leaning in around 2415 and a stick contest developing after 2422, supporting a held, dead-ball estimate through 2392. No goal is established by this sequence.

The sequence begins with a faceoff setup: the official likely holds the ball until the drop around frames 2415–2422. A prolonged, largely occluded stick battle follows through 2460. The ball then appears to work toward the left goal's right side. Red T101 is the likeliest retriever/controller near and behind the net, with white T121 defending; a defensive recovery remains possible. T101 subsequently shifts behind the goal and appears under fragment T138. Later context shows renewed crease pressure and the ball emerging onto open floor to the right at 2572. This supports continuing live play, not an intervening reset, but does not establish a particular shot, save, or goal. Locations below are mostly inferred contact regions, not direct ball sightings; radii are in original 1920×1080 pixels.

Red pressure around the left goal produces a crowded stick battle before white T136 emerges with the ball moving right. The breakout advances toward near-side white T135, who enters the opposite end along the boards, encounters red T141, and pulls back rather than driving directly at goal. T135 then appears to recycle possession leftward; a relay through T144 is possible, but the ball subsequently leaves the camera's left edge. Later context shows white possession at the left point and a renewed attempt toward the right goal. No goal, goalkeeper possession, or intervening stoppage is established.

White works the ball from the near boards to the left point, where T148 appears to shoot toward the right-hand goal. The goalkeeper drops, and the ball is subsequently visible to the right of the net; this does not establish a goal. Pursuit around the right post is followed by the ball reaching the near boards, where T144 and T146 contest it. T144 emerges moving left, with the pink ball visible ahead of his stick at 2805–2812. A return pass toward the attacking zone appears to follow. T122 and white T161 then converge on the ball; the later context supports a loose-ball deflection leftward after their encounter. No clear stoppage or official-held ball is evident. The exact right-post touch and return-pass reception remain uncertain.

Pressure at the right-hand goal produces a loose ball moving left, away from T122 and the stumbling white T161. Red T164 closes on it near the far-side lane, followed by an apparent forward feed to red T170 as the camera pans left. T170 leads the counterattack with white T169 pursuing and other players trailing. A shot or close attacking touch reaches the left goalkeeper T172 around frames 2932–2940. The goalkeeper goes down, and play subsequently stops. The ball is not clearly resolved after that contact: goalkeeper retention and a ball remaining in the goal/end area are both plausible. Neither a goal nor an assist is established by these images.

The opening goalmouth activity subsides into a continuous stoppage before the requested targets. Red players gather and exchange glove taps while white players walk away; this does not establish a goal or assist. No target provides a cleanly resolved pink/red ball. Initially, the net/crease and the goalkeeper's glove are the best-supported alternatives. As the official reaches the net, a held dead ball becomes plausible, although no pickup or transfer is clearly visible. The later leftward movement of these estimates reflects the camera panning right, not a pass. Subsequent context continues the reset and eventually pans away without revealing a restart.

This interval is a stoppage, not a continuous live-ball attack. Players leave the left goal area and move toward center while officials prepare the restart. The ball is not securely resolved; an official-held ball is plausible, with uncertainty between the goal-side and center officials in the early views. The camera then pans away to the idle opposite goalkeeper and a clock stopped at 8:30; the score display updates during this hold. On returning toward center, players are still assembling, with no restart shown. There is no evidence for moving the ball to the opposite goalkeeper or constructing a pass/shot trajectory across the camera pan.

This sequence shows a continuous stoppage and preparation for a center-court restart, not live stickhandling or a pass. The camera pans away from the waiting goalkeeper toward players gathering at center. A striped official walks toward the center line carrying the ball by hand; the held-ball observation at frame 3368 anchors the estimates before and after it. Players subsequently obscure the official's hands as they assemble for the faceoff. The later context remains consistent with restart preparation, with no demonstrated ball drop, shot, or goal. Estimated ball locations therefore follow the official's hand area, not players' stick blades or the floor.

The sequence begins with a prolonged center-floor restart: the official appears to retain the ball while players arrange themselves. The drop occurs around 3510–3518, and the stick contest sends play left. White T203 appears to collect near the far-side left lane and advance right before moving inward. The ball becomes difficult to resolve during that movement; continued T203 control is the leading interpretation, with a diagonal transfer to near-side white T192 a plausible alternative late in the sequence. By 3592–3600, play is sent toward the right end and near-side corner. Subsequent frames show red T198 retreating to retrieve, white T192 pursuing, and the red goalkeeper remaining in the crease. There is no confirmed goal or subsequent stoppage.

The center-zone white attack sends the ball deep down the near/right-side lane around frame 3600. Red T198 retreats toward the corner, with white T192 pursuing. The exact dump trajectory and first retrieval touch are obscured by camera motion and the near-side spectators. T198 appears to reach and shield the ball before T192 closes, producing a prolonged board battle. T192 subsequently appears to emerge with control along the end boards, still pressured by red, subsequently labeled T220. The later context supports this continuous corner play rather than a new possession elsewhere. Goalkeeper T212 remains positioned in the crease; there is no clear shot, goal, official-held ball, or stoppage. Most locations below are inferred contact regions, not identified ball pixels.

White T192 controls and shields the ball along the right boards, first moving left and then turning back toward the corner under pressure from red T220. T219 and T216 join the prolonged corner contest. A white attacker, apparently T192 continuing as fragment T223, emerges toward the slot; the pink ball is visible ahead of his blade at 3840 and 3848. A close-range attempt reaches goalkeeper T212, followed by an apparent rebound and possible follow-up from the left. The goalkeeper sprawls and play stops around 3878–3885. The ball is then most plausibly covered by him or hidden in the adjacent goalmouth; neither a goal nor an official holding the ball is established. The later 3930 floor sighting occurs after the stoppage and does not establish a continuous trajectory through the hidden interval.

The preceding net-front attack leaves goalkeeper T212 down, and play has stopped by the first target. Initially the ball is difficult to separate from the right-side crease traffic; its subsequent appearance favors the area near T224's stick, with the goalkeeper area remaining an early alternative. During the stoppage, the ball moves slowly left near T224's extended blade and settles on the floor in front of the goal. The approaching official bends to retrieve it around 4028–4035 and is likely holding it by 4042. The late camera pan changes image coordinates substantially. No new live pass or shot occurs in the targets, and the footage does not establish a goal or assist.

This sequence is a continuing stoppage, not an active passing or shooting play. The floor-ball proposal near the right goal at frame 4005 is followed by an official approaching, bending down at 4028–4035, and standing by 4042, strongly suggesting retrieval. The ball is subsequently most plausibly held by that official, initially tracked as T231 and later T235, while players walk toward center. No transfer or restart is visible. The camera pans away from the official after 4155; the ball then remains outside the view. Later context shows the clock unchanged at 8:06, supporting the continuing stoppage. Neither a goal nor an assist can be established from this sequence.

The supplied sequence shows a sustained stoppage, not an active attack. The clock remains at 8:06, goalkeeper T238 waits, and the camera initially excludes center court. The pan around 4282–4298 reveals players waiting around center and officials delaying the restart; later context shows a white player returning to the bench. No ball release, pass, shot, or goal is established. The ball is not cleanly visible. Once the officials enter view, retention by the central official, briefly labeled T242, is the leading hypothesis; the near-board official is a secondary possibility. These held-ball estimates are uncertain and are not floor locations.

The entire interval remains a stoppage before a center-court restart. Players wait with their sticks down while a white-team substitution occurs and the near-side official returns from the boards. The ball is most plausibly held by an official, not lying among the waiting players. Around frame 4440, a brief elevated red spot and the officials' hand movements support a short toss between officials, probably from the stationary official to the approaching one; the direction and catch are not completely resolved. The approaching official then continues toward the faceoff area. No ball drop, live possession, shot, or goal is established through frame 4492.

limitations: The sequence model sees 2-fps chronological samples in overlapping 16-second windows and occasional existing visual proposals. It infers ball state every half-second; carrier motion and camera compensation reconstruct the intermediate frames.
Contextual estimates, possession states, weights, and error radii are model hypotheses. Invisible ball positions have no independent ground truth.
The reused localization checks mostly concern previously detected positions. They do not measure accuracy of newly inferred intervals. A separate conditional audit inspects newly emitted frames.

Point-tracker appearance thresholds were compared on reused assistant labels; this is development selection, not independent validation. Seed frames and their +-3 neighbors are excluded from point checks.
All experiments here use one previously examined NBHL recording. No new cross-game generalization claim.
A camera cut resets inference. Held, airborne and height-uncertain hypotheses have no floor projection. Floor geometry remains approximate.
Output coverage includes stoppages and inferred regions. It is not visible-ball recall, possession accuracy, shot/goal accuracy, or a calibrated probability guarantee.

output_audit.scope: Systematically selected newly emitted estimates on the same five-minute NBHL recording. Conditional assistant visual audit, not independent invisible-ball ground truth. Approximate visible locations were inspected after predictions were frozen.
output_audit.reviewer: assistant visual inspection of native chronological panels
